mainTopic: Sharing the community's suffering, divine judgment, and whether a voluntary faster is a חוטא or קדוש
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of a traveler who limits his eating. It shows when the reasons מעיינא and רעבון lead to different results, and how רב פפא ate on the road. Next come rules for שני רעבון: one who goes hungry is saved from an unusual death, and marital relations are forbidden except for couples without children. A ברייתא then teaches that whoever separates from the suffering צבור will not see its comfort, while whoever suffers with it, like משה sitting on a stone, will see the נחמת צבור. The ברייתא adds that no one can sin in secret, and gives four views on who testifies against a person. It then explains the פסוק ״אל אמונה ואין עול״: צדיקים pay for small sins in עולם הזה, and רשעים are rewarded for small מצוות in עולם הזה. At death, a person confirms his deeds, signs for them, and admits the judgment was fair. Finally the גמרא returns to fasting. שמואל says one who fasts by choice is a חוטא, and רבי אלעזר says he is קדוש, both learning from the נזיר. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to challenge רבי אלעזר from another saying of his, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The practical difference between the two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The difference between the reasons מעיינא and רעבון shows up when someone travels by boat, or when someone travels from station to station.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is when he sits in a boat. Or alternatively, when he travels from one station to the next.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of an answer. Before this, the גמרא asked what practical difference there is between the two reasons for a traveler to limit his eating, and here it answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a boat there is no bumpy road, so the digestion worry (מעיינא) does not apply, but he could still run out of food (רעבון). Traveling between stations is the reverse. The road is tiring, so the digestion worry applies, but he can buy food at each stop, so the famine worry does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A station or inn along the road

steps.confusionAlert: Each case is the reverse of the other. On a boat only the רעבון reason applies. Station to station, only the מעיינא reason applies.

phrases.english: Where he is sitting in a boat.
phrases.notes: This continues the question 'what is the difference between them?' from the previous daf.

phrases.english: Alternatively, where he travels from station to station.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'מאי בינייהו' from the previous daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical case separates the reason מעיינא from the reason רעבון?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sitting in a boat, where only רעבון applies. Going from station to station, where only מעיינא applies.

steps.title: How רב פפא ate while traveling
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא ate one loaf of bread every פרסה, because he held the reason is digestion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא would eat one loaf of bread every פרסה. He held that the concern is because of the bowels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how רב פפא actually behaved on the road. It explains that his behavior follows the reason of מעיינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the concern were running out of food, he would have saved his bread. Since he held the concern is digestion, he ate in small portions spread out along the way. The גמרא does not say more about why this fits the digestion concern.

keyTerms.meaning: A parasang, a measure of distance (about 4 מיל)
He holds; he is of the opinion

phrases.english: Rav Pappa, every single parasang
would eat one loaf of bread.
He holds that it is because of the bowels.
phrases.notes: So the worry is digestion, not a shortage of food.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא כׇּל פַּרְסָה וּפַרְסָה אָכֵיל חֲדָא רִיפְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a real person's practice that follows one of the two reasons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא ate small amounts at regular intervals, following the reason מעיינא.

steps.title: Going hungry in famine years saves from an unusual death
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: one who makes himself hungry in famine years is saved from an unusual death, as the פסוק says ״ברעב פדך ממות״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Anyone who starves himself in years of famine is saved from an unusual death, as it says, 'In famine He redeemed you from death.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about famine years. Someone who has food but holds back, sharing in the community's hunger, is rewarded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves from the traveler to a general attitude. A person should feel the pain of the community during a famine and not eat his fill. The source is a פסוק in איוב, and the next step explains how the פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes himself go hungry

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Anyone who starves himself in years of famine
is saved from an unusual death,
as it is stated: 'In famine He redeemed you from death.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching on the theme of famine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who holds back from eating during famine years is saved from an unusual death.

steps.title: The verse should have said 'from famine'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the plain sense would require ״מרעב״, not ״ברעב״.
steps.simpleTranslation: It should have said 'from famine'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at one word in the פסוק. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק simply meant that God rescues you from famine, it should say ״מרעב״ (from famine). The word ״ברעב״ (through or in famine) suggests that the famine itself is the means of rescue.

phrases.english: It should have said 'from famine'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rescue from famine would be written as ״מרעב״. The word ״ברעב״ seems out of place.

steps.title: Reward for going hungry
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means that in return for going hungry during famine, a person is saved from an unusual death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: As a reward for starving himself in years of famine, he is saved from an unusual death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the unusual word ״ברעב״. It shows that this word is exactly the source for רב's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״ברעב״ means 'because of the hunger he took on.' His choosing to go hungry is what earns the rescue from death. So the odd wording becomes the proof for רב's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it is saying

steps.whatToRemember: Holding back from eating during a public famine, as an act of sharing the community's suffering, earns protection from an unusual death. This is learned from the word ״ברעב״.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:
As a reward for starving himself in years of famine,
he is saved from an unusual death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem from step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means simply 'rescue from famine' and is just oddly worded.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״ברעב״ means 'in reward for the hunger,' which is the source for רב's teaching.

steps.title: No marital relations in famine years
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש forbids marital relations during famine years, learning it from the fact that יוסף's sons were born before the famine.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: A person may not have marital relations in years of famine, as it says, 'And to Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine came.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another rule about how to act during a famine. This one is about having children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses that יוסף's sons were born before the famine. This implies that during the famine he did not have children. From this ריש לקיש learns that one should hold back from marital relations in a time of famine.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
It is forbidden for a person to have marital relations
in years of famine,
as it is stated: 'And to Joseph were born two sons'
'before the year of famine came.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second famine-time rule, added next to רב's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marital relations are forbidden during famine years.

steps.title: Childless couples are allowed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that those without children may have marital relations even in famine years.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Those who lack children may have marital relations in years of famine.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds an exception to ריש לקיש's rule. Couples who have no children are not included in the restriction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of ריש לקיש still stands in general. However, someone who has not yet fulfilled פריה ורביה may continue, because that מצוה comes first. This is an exception in how the rule is applied, not a cancellation of the rule.
steps.whatToRemember: In famine years one should hold back from food and from marital relations. Couples without children are the exception for marital relations.

phrases.english: It was taught: those lacking children
may have marital relations in years of famine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of ריש לקיש from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Childless couples are exempt from the famine-time restriction on marital relations.

steps.title: Angels mark the one who separates from the suffering community
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when ישראל suffers and one person separates himself, the two מלאכי השרת who accompany him declare that he will not see the נחמת צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When ישראל is in distress and one of them separates himself, the two ministering angels who accompany a person come, put their hands on his head, and say: 'This so-and-so, who separated himself from the community, should not see the community's comfort.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that continues the theme of acting properly in hard times. It describes the punishment of someone who cuts himself off from the community's suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps covered personal behavior during famine, such as going hungry and refraining from marital relations. This ברייתא widens the idea: any separation from the community's pain is punished. The punishment matches the sin. He separated from the pain, so he is separated from the comfort.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught.' This introduces a ברייתא.
The comfort or consolation of the community

steps.whyThisMatters: This step sets up the key phrase נחמת צבור. The section closes with that same phrase, describing the reward of the one who shares the pain.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
When the Jewish people are immersed in distress
and one of them separates himself,
the two ministering angels come
who accompany a person,
and they place their hands on his head,
phrases.notes: Like hands placed on a קרבן before it is slaughtered. It is a sign of doom.

phrases.english: and they say: This so-and-so,
who separated himself from the community,
let him not see the consolation of the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל שְׁרוּיִין בְּצַעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the earlier famine rules into a general principle about sharing the community's distress.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who separates from the suffering community will not see the community's consolation.

steps.title: Do not say 'I will go home, eat, and drink' while the community suffers
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא forbids a person from going off to enjoy himself while the צבור suffers. It applies to him the פסוקים in ישעיה about feasting and about a sin that will not be forgiven until death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: When the community is in suffering, a person should not say, 'I will go home, eat and drink, and peace be upon you, my soul.' If he does, the verse speaks about him: 'And behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen and killing sheep, eating meat and drinking wine: let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die.' What is written right after it? 'And the Lord of hosts revealed in my ears: this sin will surely not be forgiven for you until you die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא on the same theme. It describes the selfish attitude of 'let me just enjoy myself' and shows from ישעיה how severe that is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first verse describes people partying in a time of crisis. The second verse, which comes right after it, gives their punishment: their sin will not be forgiven until they die. The ברייתא reads the two verses together as cause and result.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Another ברייתא teaches.' This introduces a second ברייתא on the same theme.
'Peace be upon you, my soul.' It means: I am fine, whatever happens to others.
'What is written after it?' This points to the verse that follows.

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:
When the community is immersed in suffering,
a person should not say: I will go to my home,
and I will eat and drink,
and peace be upon you, my soul.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם עוֹשֶׂה כֵּן — עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And if he does so, the verse says about him:
"And behold joy and gladness,
slaying oxen and killing sheep,
eating meat and drinking wine;
let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die" (Isaiah 22:13),
what is written after it?
"And the Lord of hosts revealed Himself in my ears:
surely this sin will not be atoned for you
until you die" (Isaiah 22:14).

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר שָׁרוּי בְּצַעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא that supports the same theme with פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to enjoy oneself privately while the community suffers. One who does so is described by the פסוק as having a sin that will not be atoned for until he dies.

steps.title: The worse attitude of the wicked, who want the good times to last
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the previous verses describe בינונים. רשעים are worse: they hope tomorrow will be like today. Their punishment is that the צדיק is taken away before the coming evil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to here describes the level of 'middling' people. But about the level of the wicked, what is written? 'Come, I will bring wine, and we will drink our fill of strong drink, and tomorrow will be like this day.' What is written after it? 'The righteous one perishes and no one takes it to heart, that because of the coming evil the righteous one is taken away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now draws a line between two levels of bad behavior. It brings a new pair of פסוקים about רשעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בינונים at least think 'tomorrow we may die', so they sense danger but ignore it. The רשעים want the party to continue forever, as if the crisis did not exist. Their punishment is harsher: the צדיקים die early so they will not see the disaster coming on these people.

keyTerms.meaning: The level or attitude of average, middling people
The level or attitude of the wicked
The righteous one is 'gathered in', meaning he dies

steps.confusionAlert: 'עד כאן מידת בינונים' does not start a new topic. It looks back and labels the verses just quoted as describing בינונים, and only then moves on to רשעים.

phrases.english: Up to here is the attribute of middling people.
But regarding the attribute of the wicked, what is written?
"Come, I will fetch wine,
and we will fill ourselves with strong drink,
and tomorrow shall be like this day" (Isaiah 56:12),
what is written after it?
"The righteous one perishes,
and no man takes it to heart,
that because of the coming evil the righteous one is taken away" (Isaiah 57:1).

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן מִידַּת בֵּינוֹנִים. אֲבָל בְּמִדַּת רְשָׁעִים, מָה כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the previous step's verses in context and contrasts them with a worse level of behavior.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who hope the good times will continue during a crisis are רשעים. Their punishment is that the צדיקים are taken away before the disaster comes.

steps.title: A person should suffer with the community, as משה רבינו did
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the positive rule: suffer together with the צבור. It brings a source from משה רבינו, who sat on a stone during the war with עמלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a person should share in the distress of the community. We find this with משה רבינו, who made himself suffer with the community, as it says: 'And משה's hands were heavy, and they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: After describing the wrong ways to behave, the ברייתא states the right way. It begins to prove it from משה רבינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' switches from what not to do to what to do. The proof verse is quoted here. Its point, that משה chose the stone on purpose, will be drawn out in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather.' It turns from the negative to the positive instruction.
A person should share the distress of the community
'For so we find.' It introduces a precedent or proof.
'And משה's hands were heavy.' From the war with עמלק.

phrases.english: Rather, a person should be distressed together with the community,
for so we find with Moses our teacher
that he distressed himself together with the community,
as it is stated: "And Moses' hands were heavy,
and they took a stone and put it under him,
and he sat upon it" (Exodus 17:12),

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, יְצַעֵר אָדָם עִם הַצִּבּוּר, שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the negative examples to the positive instruction and begins its proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should share in the community's suffering, following משה רבינו.
steps.raayaObject: The duty to suffer with the community
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות יז:יב: משה sat on a stone during the war with עמלק

steps.title: Didn't משה have a pillow to sit on?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks a pointed question: surely משה had a pillow or cushion, so why sit on a stone?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did משה not have a single pillow or a single cushion to sit on?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question to sharpen the proof. This step sets up the next move, which explains why משה chose a stone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question shows that sitting on a stone was not because nothing else was available. It was a deliberate choice. That choice is what makes the verse a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And is it so that…?' It introduces a surprised question.

phrases.english: But did Moses not have
one pillow or one cushion
to sit upon?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי לֹא הָיָה לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה כַּר אֶחָד אוֹ כֶּסֶת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the proof verse in order to bring out its lesson.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did משה sit on a hard stone when softer seats were surely available?

steps.title: משה chose to suffer along with ישראל
steps.stepSummary: משה reasoned: since ישראל is suffering, I too will be with them in suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what משה said: Since ישראל is in suffering, I too will be with them in suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. משה sat on the stone on purpose, to share the people's pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was not fighting on the battlefield, but he still found a way to share the hardship. This turns the verse into a clear model: even someone not directly affected should feel the pain alongside the community.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what he said,' meaning his reasoning

phrases.english: Rather, this is what Moses said:
Since the Jewish people are immersed in suffering,
I too will be with them in suffering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 and completes the proof begun in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה deliberately sat on a stone to share in ישראל's suffering.

steps.title: One who suffers with the community will see its comfort
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that anyone who suffers together with the צבור merits seeing the נחמת צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anyone who makes himself suffer with the community merits to see the comfort of the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes with the reward. It is the mirror image of the punishment in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the one who separates 'will not see' the community's comfort. Here the one who shares the pain 'will see' it. The section is framed by these two matching statements.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes himself suffer or feel distress

steps.whatToRemember: Separating from the community's pain means losing its comfort. Sharing the pain, like משה on the stone, means seeing the comfort. This applies even to someone not directly suffering.

phrases.english: And anyone who distresses himself together with the community
merits and sees the consolation of the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the general reward from משה's example. It mirrors the punishment stated in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whoever shares in the community's suffering will merit seeing the community's consolation.

steps.title: Who could possibly testify against me?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises the thought of a person who sinned in secret and believes no one can testify against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And perhaps a person will say: who will testify against me?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא imagines a person who thinks a sin done in private leaves no witnesses. It is setting up the next move, where it answers this question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the ברייתא spoke about punishment and reward for the צבור. Now it blocks an escape route: someone might think judgment needs witnesses, and a private sin has none. The question exists so that the answers can show that nothing is truly hidden.

phrases.english: And perhaps a person will say:
Who will testify against me?
phrases.notes: Meaning: I acted in secret, so there are no witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the lesson of suffering with the צבור to the question of testimony in personal judgment.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who serves as a witness against a person who sinned secretly?

steps.title: The stones and beams of the house testify
steps.stepSummary: The first answer: the stones and wooden beams of a person's own house testify against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The stones of a person's house and the beams of a person's house testify against him, as it says: 'For a stone will cry out from the wall, and a beam from the wood will answer it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. Even the walls and beams of your house act as witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a פסוק in חבקוק, which describes a stone in the wall crying out and a beam answering it. The point is that the very place where you sin 'saw' what you did. A private room is not truly private.

keyTerms.meaning: a beam or crosspiece of wood

phrases.english: The stones of a person's house

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹרוֹת בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מְעִידִים בּוֹ,
phrases.english: and the beams of a person's house testify against him,
as it says: 'For a stone will cry out from the wall,
and a beam from the wood will answer it' (Habakkuk 2:11).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The stones and beams of his house testify, based on חבקוק ב:יא.

steps.title: The two accompanying angels testify
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי שילא says the two מלאכי השרת who go with a person testify against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי שילא say: the two ministering angels who accompany a person testify against him, as it says: 'For He will command His angels for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to 'who testifies?' is given. דבי רבי שילא say it is the two angels that go with every person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים says ה׳ commands His angels to guard you in all your ways. If they are with you everywhere, they see everything you do. The guards who protect you are also the witnesses to your actions.

keyTerms.meaning: the school (study house) of רבי שילא

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Sheila say:
The two ministering angels
who accompany a person,
they testify against him,
as it says: 'For He will command His angels for you' (Psalms 91:11).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from step 16 to the same question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two accompanying angels are the witnesses.

steps.title: A person's own soul testifies
steps.stepSummary: רבי חידקא says a person's own נשמה testifies against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חידקא says: a person's soul testifies against him, as it says: 'From the one who lies in your bosom, guard the openings of your mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer is given. רבי חידקא says the witness is the person's own נשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in מיכה warns you to guard your mouth even from 'the one who lies in your bosom.' רבי חידקא reads this as the נשמה, which lives inside you and knows everything. The witness here is not outside you at all.
steps.confusionAlert: In its simple meaning, the פסוק speaks about a wife or a close companion. רבי חידקא reads 'the one who lies in your bosom' as a hint to the נשמה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥidka says:

phrases.aramaic: נִשְׁמָתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם הִיא מְעִידָה עָלָיו,
phrases.english: A person's soul, it testifies against him,
as it says: 'From the one who lies in your bosom,
guard the openings of your mouth' (Micah 7:5).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third answer to the question of step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person's own נשמה is the witness.

steps.title: A person's own limbs testify
steps.stepSummary: יש אומרים: a person's own limbs testify against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: a person's limbs testify against him, as it says: 'You are My witnesses, says ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth answer is given. The limbs of the body that did the sin are themselves the witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ישעיה says 'You are My witnesses.' It is read as saying that the person himself, meaning his own body, is ה׳'s witness. The hands and feet that did the act will testify to it.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four views on who testifies against a secret sinner: the house (stones and beams), the two angels, the נשמה, or the limbs. All four agree on one thing: no sin is truly hidden.

phrases.english: And some say:
A person's limbs testify against him,
as it says: 'You are My witnesses, says the Lord' (Isaiah 43:10).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the fourth and final answer to the question of step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person's own limbs are the witnesses.

steps.title: The righteous are punished in this world for small sins
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains אל אמונה: just as רשעים are punished in עולם הבא even for a small sin, צדיקים are punished in עולם הזה for a small sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A faithful God, without iniquity.' 'A faithful God': just as the wicked are punished in עולם הבא even for a light sin they do, so too the righteous are punished in עולם הזה for a light sin they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא quotes a new פסוק about ה׳'s fair judgment and explains its first half. It teaches that ה׳ collects even for small sins from everyone, but at different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אל אמונה means ה׳ is exact and lets nothing slide. A small sin is never ignored, whether the person is a רשע or a צדיק. The difference is timing: the צדיק pays here in עולם הזה, so that his עולם הבא can stay clean.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean צדיקים are punished more than רשעים. Both are held accountable for small sins. The צדיק simply pays in this world, which protects his share in עולם הבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a classic explanation for why good people sometimes suffer in this world.

phrases.english: 'A faithful God and without iniquity' (Deuteronomy 32:4).
'A faithful God':

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנִּפְרָעִין מִן הָרְשָׁעִים לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
phrases.english: just as punishment is collected from the wicked in the World to Come
even for a light sin that they do,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ נִפְרָעִין מִן הַצַּדִּיקִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: so too punishment is collected from the righteous in this world
for a light sin that they do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who testifies to how the judgment itself works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים are punished in עולם הזה for their small sins.

steps.title: The wicked are rewarded in this world for small מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains ואין עול: just as צדיקים are rewarded in עולם הבא even for a small מצוה, רשעים are rewarded in עולם הזה even for a small מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And without iniquity': just as reward is paid to the righteous in עולם הבא even for a light מצוה they do, so too reward is paid to the wicked in עולם הזה even for a light מצוה they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the second half of the פסוק‎. ה׳ never cheats anyone of reward, not even a רשע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ואין עול means there is no unfairness: every מצוה gets paid. The צדיק receives his reward in עולם הבא. The רשע is paid in עולם הזה, so his account is closed here. This mirrors step 20 exactly.
steps.whatToRemember: ה׳ is exact both ways. צדיקים pay for small sins in עולם הזה and get full reward in עולם הבא. רשעים get paid for small מצוות in עולם הזה and face their punishment in עולם הבא. This explains why צדיקים sometimes suffer and רשעים sometimes prosper.

phrases.english: 'And without iniquity':

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּשַׁלְּמִין שָׂכָר לַצַּדִּיקִים לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
phrases.english: just as reward is paid to the righteous in the World to Come
even for a light מצוה that they do,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ מְשַׁלְּמִין שָׂכָר לָרְשָׁעִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
phrases.english: so too reward is paid to the wicked in this world
even for a light מצוה that they do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the פסוק begun in step 20, now on the side of reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רשעים receive reward in עולם הזה for their small מצוות.

steps.title: At death, a person's deeds are read out and he signs for them
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains ״צדיק וישר הוא״: when a person dies, all his deeds are laid out before him. He confirms each one and signs, as the פסוק in איוב says.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He is just and right." They said: When a person leaves this world for his eternal home, all his deeds are listed in front of him. They tell him: 'You did this and this, in this place, on this day.' He says: 'Yes.' They tell him: 'Sign!' And he signs, as it says: "He makes the hand of every man sign."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its line-by-line reading of the פסוק from Steps 20–21 and now explains the last phrase, ״צדיק וישר הוא״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 20–21 explained אל אמונה and ואין עול. Now ״צדיק וישר״ is shown in action: Heaven's judgment is so fair that the person himself confirms every detail and signs it. This ties to Steps 15–19, which asked who testifies against a person and gave four answers. Here the person ends up confirming it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: His eternal home (the World to Come or the grave)

phrases.english: "He is just and right": they said:
phrases.notes: Third part of the פסוק in דברים לב:ד

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁעַת פְּטִירָתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם לְבֵית עוֹלָמוֹ
phrases.english: At the time a person departs to his eternal home
all his deeds are listed out before him,
and they say to him: You did such and such
phrases.notes: Sefaria understands the deeds themselves as speaking

phrases.english: in such a place, on such a day,
and he says: Yes,
and they say to him: Sign! And he signs.
as it says: "He makes the hand of every man sign."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving to the next phrase of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At death a person sees all his deeds, confirms them, and signs for them.

steps.title: The person even admits the judgment was fair
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the person does more than sign. He declares that he was judged well, fulfilling the פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but he accepts the judgment on himself and says to them: 'You judged me well,' to fulfill what is written: "So that You will be justified when You speak."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a further point: the person openly agrees that the judgment against him is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Signing only confirms the facts. Saying יפה דנתוני also agrees that the verdict is fair. This finishes the meaning of ״צדיק וישר״: even the one being judged declares ה׳'s judgment just.

keyTerms.meaning: Not only that, but even more
Accepts the judgment on himself as just

steps.whatToRemember: ״צדיק וישר״: at death a person confirms his deeds, signs for them, and admits the judgment was fair.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁמַּצְדִּיק עָלָיו אֶת הַדִּין,
phrases.english: And not only that, but he accepts the judgment on himself as just,
and says to them: You judged me well,
to fulfill what is written: "So that You will be justified in Your words."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא שֶׁמַּצְדִּיק עָלָיו אֶת הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further stage on top of Step 22: signing, and then admitting the verdict is fair.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person declares the judgment fair, fulfilling ״למען תצדק בדברך״.

steps.title: שמואל: one who fasts is called a sinner
steps.stepSummary: Returning to fasting, שמואל rules that anyone who sits in a תענית is called a חוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Anyone who sits in a fast is called a sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the אגדה and goes back to the main subject of the מסכת, fasting. שמואל gives a surprising ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that causing yourself pain without need is wrong, so a person who fasts on his own is labeled a חוטא. The next step shows which תנא this view is based on.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sits in (observes) a fast

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is talking about a person who takes on a fast by choice. He is not talking about the fixed fasts that everyone must keep, or public fasts declared in a crisis.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Anyone who sits in a fast is called a sinner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל הַיּוֹשֵׁב בְּתַעֲנִית נִקְרָא חוֹטֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא goes back from the אגדה to the laws and ideas of fasting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who fasts by choice is called a חוטא.

steps.title: שמואל's source: the נזיר 'sinned' by holding back from wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says שמואל follows רבי אלעזר הקפר. He reads the פסוק about the נזיר's atonement to mean that the נזיר sinned by causing himself pain through avoiding wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds like this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר הקפר ברבי says, why does the פסוק say "And he will atone for him for having sinned regarding the soul"? With what soul did this person sin? Rather, he caused himself pain by holding back from wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a תנא whose view supports שמואל's ruling and brings his reading of a פסוק about the נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזיר brings a קרבן to atone, and the פסוק says he 'sinned regarding the נפש'. Since he did not hurt anyone else, רבי אלעזר הקפר explains that the sin was against his own self: he denied himself wine. So holding back from permitted pleasure can count as a sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק say this?

phrases.english: He holds like this tanna, as it was taught:
Rabbi Elazar HaKappar the Great says,
What does the verse come to teach:
"And he will atone for him for having sinned regarding the soul",
With what soul did this one sin?
Rather, he caused himself pain by holding back from wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source of שמואל's view from Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that one who fasts is called a חוטא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר הקפר's reading of ״חטא על הנפש״ about the נזיר.

steps.title: קל וחומר: someone who avoids everything is surely a sinner
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר הקפר finishes with a קל וחומר. If the נזיר, who only avoids wine, is called a חוטא, then one who fasts from everything surely is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a קל וחומר? If this one, who only held back from wine, is called a sinner, then one who holds back from every single thing, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא takes the lesson about the נזיר and applies it to a person who fasts, using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזיר is the 'light' case, since he avoids only one thing. The faster is the 'heavy' case, since he avoids all food and drink. If the light case is already a sin, the heavy case must be one too, which gives שמואל's ruling exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: A reasoning from a lighter case to a heavier one

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל and רבי אלעזר הקפר: the נזיר avoided only wine and is called a חוטא, so one who fasts from everything is surely a חוטא.

phrases.english: And are these matters not an a fortiori:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה זֶה, שֶׁלֹּא צִיעֵר עַצְמוֹ אֶלָּא מִן הַיַּיִן —
phrases.english: If this one, who only pained himself by avoiding wine,
is called a sinner,
one who pains himself by avoiding each and every thing,
all the more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof from Step 25 by moving from the נזיר to the faster.
steps.raayaObject: One who fasts is called a חוטא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the נזיר, who is called a חוטא for avoiding wine alone.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: one who fasts is called holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר disagrees. Because the פסוק calls the נזיר קדוש, a person who fasts from everything is surely called קדוש, by the same kind of קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: he is called holy, as it says: "He shall be holy, letting the hair of his head grow long." If this one, who only held back from one thing, is called holy, then one who holds back from everything, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opposite view. The same נזיר and the same kind of קל וחומר now lead to the conclusion that a faster is קדוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר focuses on a different פסוק about the נזיר, which calls him קדוש. He then runs the same קל וחומר: avoiding one thing earns the title קדוש, so avoiding everything earns it even more. The disagreement is over which description of the נזיר shows what holding back really is.

keyTerms.meaning: Letting the hair grow long (a law of the נזיר)
One who vowed to avoid wine, haircuts, and טומאת מת

steps.confusionAlert: This רבי אלעזר is a different person from רבי אלעזר הקפר in Step 25. Both build on the same נזיר with the same קל וחומר structure, but they reach opposite conclusions.
steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת: שמואל and רבי אלעזר הקפר say one who fasts is a חוטא, based on ״חטא על הנפש״. רבי אלעזר says he is קדוש, based on ״קדוש יהיה״. Both learn it from the נזיר with a קל וחומר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת shapes the attitude of the rest of the sugya toward voluntary fasting: is self-denial a fault or a mark of holiness?

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: he is called holy,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״קָדוֹשׁ יִהְיֶה גַּדֵּל פֶּרַע שְׂעַר רֹאשׁוֹ״.
phrases.english: as it says: "He shall be holy, letting the locks of the hair of his head grow long."

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה זֶה, שֶׁלֹּא צִיעֵר עַצְמוֹ אֶלָּא מִדָּבָר אֶחָד —
phrases.english: If this one, who only pained himself by avoiding one thing,
is called holy,
one who pains himself by avoiding everything,
all the more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to שמואל and רבי אלעזר הקפר, using the same structure of proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who fasts is called קדוש, learned by a קל וחומר from the נזיר.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל: the נזיר is called holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שמואל can call a faster a חוטא, since the פסוק calls the נזיר קדוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל, the נזיר is called 'holy'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי אלעזר's פסוק against שמואל. If the נזיר is called holy, how can holding back from pleasure be a sin?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל built his view on the word חוטא about the נזיר. But the תורה also calls the נזיר קדוש, which seems to praise him. So שמואל has to explain that word.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to שמואל (introduces a problem for his view)

phrases.english: And according to Shmuel,
but he (the nazir) is called holy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי אלעזר's source against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that one who fasts is a חוטא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls the נזיר קדוש, which suggests that holding back is praiseworthy and not sinful.

steps.title: Answer: the holiness refers to the hair
steps.stepSummary: For שמואל, the word קדוש describes the נזיר's growing hair, not the person.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is referring to the growing of the hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for שמואל. The word 'holy' in the פסוק is about the נזיר's hair, not the נזיר himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'he shall be holy, letting the locks of his hair grow.' שמואל reads 'holy' as going with the hair. So the person himself is never praised as holy, and calling him a חוטא still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The growing of the hair (of a נזיר)

phrases.english: That one
is referring to the growing of the locks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: קדוש describes only the hair, so the person can still be a חוטא.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי אלעזר: the נזיר is called a sinner
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא flips the question. How can רבי אלעזר call a faster holy, if the נזיר is called a חוטא?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי אלעזר, the נזיר is called a sinner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses שמואל's פסוק against רבי אלעזר. The same kind of attack is aimed at the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says that holding back makes a person holy. But the תורה says the נזיר brings a קרבן because 'he sinned.' So רבי אלעזר has to explain that word.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Elazar,
but he is called a sinner!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 28, now aimed at רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that one who fasts is called קדוש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls the נזיר a חוטא, which suggests that holding back is sinful.

steps.title: Answer: the sin is becoming impure
steps.stepSummary: For רבי אלעזר, the word חוטא refers only to a נזיר who made himself טמא from a dead body.
steps.simpleTranslation: That refers to one who made himself impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי אלעזר. The 'sin' in the פסוק is not about avoiding wine. It is about a נזיר who became טמא מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about 'he sinned' appears in the section about a נזיר who became impure from a dead body, which is forbidden to him. So his sin was the טומאה, not his נזירות. Avoiding wine itself stays holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity from contact with a dead body

steps.whatToRemember: Each side explains the other's word about the נזיר. For שמואל, 'holy' means the hair. For רבי אלעזר, 'sinner' means a נזיר who became טמא.

phrases.english: That one
is one who rendered himself impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the פסוק to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חוטא refers to every נזיר because he avoided wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: חוטא refers only to a נזיר who became טמא מת.

steps.title: Did רבי אלעזר really say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge רבי אלעזר from another statement of his. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And did רבי אלעזר really say this? But didn't רבי אלעזר say: A person should always consider himself...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. It starts quoting a different teaching of רבי אלעזר that seems to go against praising fasting, and the quote finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר just said that one who fasts is holy. Now the גמרא brings another saying of his that seems to point the other way. This creates a possible contradiction within רבי אלעזר's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say? (opens a contradiction)

steps.confusionAlert: The quote is not finished here. Wait for the next passage to see what רבי אלעזר said and why it is a problem.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Elazar say this?
But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
A person should always consider himself

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי אלעזר from the פסוק, the גמרא now tests him against his own words.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's view that one who fasts is called קדוש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another teaching of רבי אלעזר (finished on the next amud) seems to go against praising fasting.
